newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: De Beers says early days for Russia talks.
newsitem.headline: De Beers says early days for Russia talks.

text.p: South Africa's De Beers said on Friday it is still early days for it to enter into any deals with other Moscow gem producers after the expiry of its diamond agreement with Russia on New Year's Eve.

De Beers said in December the expiry of its pact with Russia would leave it free to negotiate favourable terms of sale with smaller individual suppliers within that country on a "willing buyer, willing seller" basis.
"It is only January 3...," De Beers spokesman Andrew Cumine told Reuters on Friday.
"It is not like walking into a shop and buying sweets off the counter."
De Beers' gem marketing agreement with Moscow expired on December 31 after the government missed a deadline to approve a draft accord on diamond exports.
"The contractual agreement to purchase diamonds from the Russians expired on December 31," Cumine confirmed.
He said De Beers, which has said it is hopeful a new deal will be signed this year, had not yet resumed formal talks with Russian authorities.
Russian Finance Minister Alexander Livshits was reported as saying last week that Moscow believed a deal on diamond exports with the South African group was "essential" and could be signed this year.
Cumine said De Beers had seen the press reports "but as far as formal talks are concerned those have not happened yet."

De Beers controls about three quarters of the world diamond market and Russia accounts for about 25 percent of all rough gems De Beers sells. A five-year deal expired in December 1995 and was replaced by a memorandum signed in February 1996.
De Beers set the end-of-year deadline after being frustrated over Moscow's lack of response on the new trade deal and irritated by gem exports outside the interim scheme.

Despite the broken agreement Russia's diamond company Almazy Rossii-Sakha, or ARS, which is De Beers' negotiating partner and Russia's near-monopoly producer, has said Moscow would eventually negotiate a deal and quitting the cartel is not an option.
